Reseña de PAC-MAN 256

PAC-MAN 256 es una reinterpretación muy creativa y moderna del clásico PAC-MAN que logra transformar una vieja falla histórica del juego original en la base de una experiencia arcade extremadamente adictiva.

El juego toma inspiración del famoso “nivel 256” roto del PAC-MAN clásico y lo convierte en una amenaza constante conocida como el Glitch, una ola de corrupción digital que persigue al jugador mientras avanza por un laberinto infinito.

Uno de los mayores puntos fuertes es justamente cómo adapta la fórmula clásica a una experiencia endless runner mucho más dinámica y rápida.

El gameplay mantiene la esencia de comer puntos y escapar de fantasmas, pero ahora agrega mejoras temporales, habilidades especiales y progresión constante.

Los power-ups son especialmente entretenidos. Láseres, tornados, explosiones gigantes y muchas otras habilidades convierten las partidas en algo mucho más caótico y espectacular.

Visualmente el juego mezcla muy bien estilo retro pixelado con efectos modernos llenos de colores y luces.

La música y sonidos clásicos de PAC-MAN también fueron modernizados correctamente sin perder identidad nostálgica.

El ritmo de las partidas funciona excelente para sesiones rápidas y casuales, haciendo muy fácil jugar “solo una partida más”.

La progresión y desbloqueo de mejoras ayudan bastante a mantener interés durante muchas horas.

Sin embargo, después de bastante tiempo el gameplay puede volverse repetitivo debido a la estructura infinita de las partidas.

Algunas mejoras también se sienten claramente más útiles que otras, afectando un poco el balance.

Además, aunque el concepto del Glitch es creativo, eventualmente gran parte de las partidas terminan desarrollándose de forma bastante similar.

Aun así, PAC-MAN 256 sigue siendo una de las reinterpretaciones modernas más inteligentes y entretenidas de un clásico arcade histórico.

Until recently, the last PAC-MAN game I played came out in 1987 so I purchased PAC-MAN 256 along with some other newer ones to see what I've missed.  

It's a decent roguelite that offers meta progression by allowing you to use coins to buy and upgrade various powerups.  You can find coins in the maze but the game will also reward you with coin packages if you keep playing.  Completing random missions also nets more coins. 

Unlike older PAC-MAN titles, there are no levels in this game.  Instead, it's an endless runner that's all about getting the highest score possible.  The maze does change as you progress, however, and there are a couple of new ghost types, so the gameplay stays fresh for awhile.  

There is also a moving glitch (the game's name is based on a glitch that occurs in level 256 of the original PAC-MAN) that will instantly kill you if you get caught in it, so you're forced to move forward and plan accordingly.  Fortunately, there are a number of useful powerups along with the power pills that can make clearing ghosts a lot easier.  I generally found a use for most of these powerups but some are more helpful than others.  

Getting most of the achievements isn't too difficult but fully upgrading all the powerups is going to be a grind and I haven't completed that yet.  This game is fun enough that I will return to it eventually.  

PAC-MAN 256 is one of the better PAC-MAN games available on Steam.  It's more fun than several of the older ones I played long ago so I highly recommend it.

[h1] Awarded the best mobile game of 2015; the award stands up to its name. [/h1]

PAC-MAN 256 surely was something for the time: as it was the first ever game in the PAC-MAN franchise to profit off the infamous "Level 256" killscreen from the original 1980 arcade game (unless you count the game with the same name, "Pac-Man 256", which is the original game but the player starts at level 255 for easier access to the infamous glitched level.)

[h2] Gameplay [/h2]

The core gameplay is very simple: it's an endless runner, which means you go forward for an indefinite amount of time while dodging all of the ghosts you come along the way with racking up an high score (like an arcade game) and outrunning the glitch that slowly devours the maze behind you. There's nothing wrong with the core gameplay itself, after all, it's Pac-Man. You CANNOT possibly go wrong with Pac-Man.

[h2] Power-Ups & Replayability(?) [/h2]

This is also the very first Pac-Man game to have added a new select amount of power-ups that isn't the Energizer/Power-Pellet or some variant of it. Every power-up has its niche use, whethever you're actively going for more points by destroying ghosts or passively avoiding them.
Something you'll quickly find out, is that some of the later power-ups you unlock have a tendency to be upgraded versions of previous power-ups; for example: Laser shoots a laser (duh) out of Pac-Man's mouth in a straight line, meanwhile Optics shoots a laser out of Pac-Man's mouth that rebounds off the wall it hits to the left/right and Regen being the same thing as Magnet, except it regenerates the Pac-Dots in its range. Speaking of unlocks..
Unlike the original mobile version, whereas you unlock a power-up and you have to wait a certain amount of time to unlock the next one, (which effectively lets you stop playing the game until the next power-up is unlocked) you have to actively work to unlock the power-ups. Instead of relying on a timer that ticks down even if you're outside of the game, the game now relies on you eating an specifc total amount of Pac-Dots during runs to unlock the next power-up, which is a nice way to incentivize to play more.

[h2] Tediousness [/h2]

The only (and major) flaw this game has is how boring/tedious it can get quickly, especially after you 100% the game by upgrading all the power-ups, since there is now nothing else to do other than go for a tremendously high score. This is to be expected, since the game was designed to be primarily an arcade-like game, and most of them, one of them being Pac-Man himself is that it simply never ends until the player dies and their high score is set until some other person comes around to try and beat that said high score.

[h2] Multiplayer [/h2]

The console and PC versions of the game are the only versions where the game has Co-Op Multiplayer. Personally, I haven't played it (except for the one time to get the one achievement I didn't even know existed) since literally no one else in my friends list has the game in their library, plus, Steam Remote Play isn't exactly the best thing in the world, but hey, whaddya know. From the videos I've seen online, co-op seems to be wicked fun.

[h2] Conclusion [/h2]

The game is insanely good, and could even be addicting should you somehow not get bored of it even after doing everything there is (refer to the people that have 200,000+ as their high score)

PAC-MAN 256 is a confident and energetic reimagining of a timeless classic, taking the familiar maze-chase foundation and transforming it into a modern, endlessly replayable experience. Developed collaboratively by BANDAI NAMCO Studios Vancouver, Hipster Whale, and 3 Sprockets, and published by BANDAI NAMCO Entertainment, the game builds its entire identity around one of gaming’s most famous glitches. What was once a technical failure at level 256 in the original arcade Pac-Man becomes the central antagonist here, a creeping corruption that constantly pushes players forward and fundamentally reshapes how Pac-Man is played.

Instead of discrete stages, PAC-MAN 256 unfolds as a vertically scrolling, infinite maze. The screen relentlessly advances upward, forcing Pac-Man to keep moving lest he be consumed by the advancing glitch from below. This single design change injects constant tension into the experience, turning the traditionally methodical maze navigation into a high-pressure survival challenge. Familiar mechanics like eating dots, baiting ghosts, and grabbing fruit are still present, but they now exist within a far more aggressive rhythm where hesitation can be fatal.

Ghost behavior retains echoes of the original personalities while introducing new variations that complicate decision-making. Classic threats mix with unpredictable enemies that teleport, block paths, or behave erratically under pressure. Combined with procedurally generated layouts, this ensures that no two runs play out the same way. Even experienced Pac-Man players must constantly adapt, reading the maze on the fly and choosing whether to clear dots methodically or sprint for survival when the glitch closes in.

One of the game’s defining strengths is its extensive power-up system. Unlike traditional Pac-Man, where the power pellet temporarily flips the hunter-prey dynamic, PAC-MAN 256 equips players with a rotating selection of special abilities that can drastically alter playstyle. Lasers cut through entire rows of ghosts, tornadoes scatter enemies, giant Pac-Men plow through obstacles, and time-manipulating effects buy precious seconds. Choosing which power-ups to equip and learning how to use them efficiently becomes a strategic layer that deepens the otherwise simple controls. High-level play revolves around mastering these tools and chaining them together under pressure.

Progression is driven by coins collected during runs, which unlock new power-ups, upgrades, and cosmetic themes. This creates a steady sense of forward momentum even when runs end abruptly. While the core objective never changes—survive as long as possible—the expanding toolkit encourages experimentation and keeps the loop engaging. Short sessions are easy to jump into, yet the constant lure of a better run or a smarter power-up combination makes the game remarkably hard to put down.

The Steam version adds a particularly enjoyable dimension through local cooperative multiplayer. Up to four players can share the same maze, reviving one another and contributing to a collective score. This mode transforms the experience from a solitary test of reflexes into a chaotic, laughter-filled scramble where coordination and sacrifice matter just as much as individual skill. The screen fills with ghosts, effects, and near-misses, creating moments that feel closer to a party game without losing the core arcade challenge.

Visually, the game strikes a balance between nostalgia and clarity. Bright colors, clean lines, and instantly readable enemy designs keep the action understandable even as the screen fills with chaos. The glitch itself is a constant visual reminder of the game’s concept, distorting the maze in unsettling ways that reinforce urgency without becoming visually overwhelming. Sound design complements this with familiar Pac-Man cues mixed with modern effects that heighten tension as danger escalates.

That said, the game’s focus on a single endless mode may eventually feel limiting for some players. There are no traditional campaigns or structured challenges beyond score chasing and unlock progression. For players who thrive on variety or long-form objectives, the experience may feel repetitive over extended periods. However, this limitation is also part of the game’s purity: PAC-MAN 256 is unapologetically arcade-driven, built around mastery, reflexes, and replayability rather than narrative or mode diversity.

Ultimately, PAC-MAN 256 succeeds because it understands both the legacy it draws from and the expectations of modern arcade design. It respects the simplicity of the original while injecting urgency, spectacle, and strategic depth through its endless format and inventive power-ups. Whether played solo in pursuit of a personal best or cooperatively amid controlled chaos, it stands as one of the most effective modern reinterpretations of a classic arcade icon, proving that even a decades-old maze can feel thrilling when the rules are pushed just far enough.

Rating: 9/10

Um dos pontos mais fortes do jogo:

Laser, tornado, gigante, tempo lento, entre outros.

É possível combinar power-ups, criando jogadas espetaculares.

🎨 Gráficos e som

Visual em pixel art moderno, respeitando o estilo clássico.

Animações fluidas e efeitos visuais chamativos.

Trilha sonora e efeitos sonoros nostálgicos, mas atualizados.

🧠 Fator viciante

Partidas rápidas incentivam o famoso “só mais uma vez”.

Sistema de pontuação, missões e progressão mantém o jogador engajado.

Ideal tanto para jogadores casuais quanto para os mais competitivos.

本作は、古典的な迷路型ゲームをエンドレスランナー形式へと再構築したタイトルです。プレイヤーはプロシージャル生成された通路を進行し、背後から迫るグリッチ状の崩壊を回避しながら距離、サバイバル、スコアを追求します。

パワーエサおよびゴースト連鎖が得点の主軸であり、連続してゴーストを捕食することでスコア倍率が上昇します。レーザーや凍結効果などのパワーアップは短時間の優位性を提供し、適切な活用により走行時間が延長されます。

ゴーストの種類によって行動パターンが異なり、一部は執拗に追跡し、他は不規則に移動します。パターンの読解により袋小路の回避が可能であり、ゲーム速度の上昇とともに難易度も増加します。

進行要素として新規パワーアップやアップグレードが解禁され、戦略性や生存性を向上させます。これにより中期的な目標設定が成立し、アンロック速度は適度に調整されています。

ビジュアルはレトロ調のピクセルアートとグリッチ演出を組み合わせ、腐食範囲の拡大に伴い画面は暗転しますが、視認性は維持されています。サウンドキューは脅威および強化状態を明確に通知します。

本作は短時間のハイスコアセッションを志向するユーザーに適合します。深度はパターン認識とパワーアップの使用タイミングに集約されており、現代的な変動要素を伴うアーケード的緊張感を提供します。

Recentemente me deu uma baita vontade de jogar os jogos da série PAC-MAN, tudo por conta de uma vaga lembrança do PAC-MAN World 3, que joguei no PS2. Então vamos lá!

 Bom, PAC-MAN 256 é uma junção da saga Pac-Man com a desenvolvedora Hipster Whale, criadora de Crossing Road, um game que eu joguei muito, e essa junção acabou criando um game meio... entediante.

 O game tem o estilo Maze, mas dessa vez, sem fim, famoso endless, você joga com o objetivo de conquistar a maior pontuação possível, enquanto desvia de novos tipos de fantasmas, e é introduzido ao carro chefe deste game, os Power-ups!

 Os Power-ups são legais, com 2 focos, Power-ups ofensivos, e Power-ups defensivos, cada um com um tipo de ação, e que são upados até o lvl8, através de moedinhas que você coleta durante a gameplay.

 O game consegue te entreter por 2h ou 3h, mas acaba ficando repetitivo, O grind até os últimos power-ups é extremamente desnecessário, o que acaba tornando a gameplay entediante afim de desbloquear todos os power-ups, que são o diferencial do jogo.

 É um joguinho legal, mas entendia rápido.
